The *Aparalakuṇḍakabhaddiya Sutta* (Ud 7.5) is a discourse found in the seventh chapter of the *Udāna* (PTS Ud 76) [SuttaCentral]. The text centres on the venerable Lakuṇḍaka Bhaddiya and addresses the themes of inner and outer beauty [SuttaCentral]. In later paracanonical exegesis, the discourse is referenced in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2, *Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi*) [SuttaCentral]. Sixteen translations into thirteen modern languages are catalogued on SuttaCentral, including an English version by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Curated passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral include the *Paṭhamakāmabhūsutta* of the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 41.5) as well as poetic parallels in the *Paśyavarga* (chapter 27) of several recensions of the *Udānavarga*, notably the Sanskrit editions (UV 27, UVS 27), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 27), and Chinese versions in T 212.28 and T 213.27 [SuttaCentral]. In terms of textual reuse, DharmaNexus detects significant Pali-internal parallels, most prominently with the *Bhikkhu Saṁyutta* (SN 21, sharing an extensive passage from §1.3–5.1 with SN 21.6), as well as formulaic shared phrasing with the *Kīṭāgiri Sutta* (MN 70), the *Bodhirājakumāra Sutta* (MN 85), the *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), and its companion text, the *Paṭhamalakuṇḍakabhaddiya Sutta* (Ud 7.1) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text with a matching segment in the Chinese translation of the *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99, fascicle 38) [DharmaNexus].
